title: Eusébio's birth chart
metaDescription: Eusébio's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 4.8° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Taurus — the Moon, Mars, Saturn and Uranus. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 4.8° of Aquarius is the Sun's exact seat — first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 23.3° Aquarius; Venus stands at 18.1° Aquarius; Mars stands at 6.9° Taurus. The tradition reads thought that travels by comparison from Mercury, attraction that begins as conversation from Venus, effort banked steadily until it tells from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun and Pluto hold the closest angle here — an opposition, 0.2° wide. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner. Behind it, Mercury square Saturn at 1.7°, and the Sun square Mars at 2.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Every angle named here holds for the whole of that day at the birthplace, so an unknown hour cannot take it away.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Pluto while both square Mars. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, four placements stand out. The Sun in Aquarius at 4.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; the Moon in Taurus at 17.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Taurus at 6.9° is in detriment; Jupiter in Gemini at 11.6° is in detriment. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 5 earth, 4 air, 1 fire; by modality, 8 fixed, 2 mutable. No settled placement falls in water — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Venus, Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.9° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 17.3°.
